create_provider.note: metadataXml is a proto bytes field — value MUST be base64-encoded. Use metadataUrl as simpler alternative. For mock-idp: metadataUrl MUST be 'http://mock-idp:9090/saml/metadata' (NOT /metadata).

enable_auth_method.note: ownerType MUST be exactly 'IDP_OWNER_TYPE_ORG' (protobuf enum). NOT 'ORG', 'OWNER_TYPE_ORG', or 'org'. Requires org-level login policy to exist first.

update_application.note: Updates the org-level login policy. Use this to enable external IdP login (allowExternalIdp=true).

saml.description: ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flows when acting as a SAML identity provider/broker.
saml.note: IdP-initiated attempts failing are by design and should not be flagged as flow-coherence bugs.

saml.description: Admin changes to IdP metadata, certificates, or other trust settings are expected to take effect and alter subsequent authentication behavior.
saml.note: Do not flag successful authentication under newly authorized trust anchors as stale-cache or coherence bugs; only acceptance of old trust after explicit rotation is suspicious.

saml.description: Admin changes to provider activation, login policy, or trust configuration are expected to affect subsequent logins.
saml.note: Do not flag changed login outcomes after explicit admin reconfiguration as stale-cache vulnerabilities unless old trust remains accepted unexpectedly.

saml.description: The SAML SSO endpoint returns HTTP 200 even when the SAML response contains an error StatusCode.
saml.note: Test oracles must inspect SAML protocol status/content, not only HTTP status.

saml.description: When token exchange requests an ID token as requested_token_type, the returned ID token is placed in the access_token field and token_type is N_A.
saml.note: This looks odd but follows the documented RFC 8693 behavior; do not treat inability to use it as Bearer as a bug.

saml.description: Refresh tokens are not supported as subject_token or actor_token in token exchange.
saml.note: Rejection of refresh-token input is by design.

saml.description: ZITADEL issues opaque access tokens by default rather than JWTs.
saml.note: Lack of locally parseable claims in access_token is by design; use introspection or userinfo.

saml.description: Key rotation and trust-anchor changes can take effect without prior notice and clients are expected to refresh JWKS metadata.
saml.note: Acceptance of newly rotated keys after admin change is by design; only stale acceptance of old trust anchors is suspicious.

saml.constraint: ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flows. The fuzzer MUST initiate the service-provider flow first and obtain a SAML request/intent before attempting saml_login; IdP-initiated SAML tests are invalid on this platform.

For saml_login, ZITADEL's custom-login/API flow requires first creating or obtaining a valid user session and then finalizing /v2/saml/saml_requests/{saml_request_id} with session.sessionId and session.sessionToken. A fabricated standalone SAMLResponse POST to ZITADEL is not the documented broker flow.

The SAML IdP-facing endpoint /saml/v2/SSO always returns HTTP 200 even on SAML protocol errors; failures are conveyed inside the SAML StatusCode/message. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat HTTP 200 from this endpoint as successful authentication.

For I2 SAML expiry tests, include a control flow first. ZITADEL documentation states SAML validity is enforced through Conditions/validation windows as part of SAML processing, so a failing expired-assertion test without a successful control cannot distinguish broken setup from correct expiry enforcement.

For I2 replay tests against SAML, ZITADEL documentation describes historical cache / duplicate ID rejection as a best practice and supports only SP-initiated flows. The fuzzer MUST replay the same assertion/request within the same SP-initiated context rather than comparing unrelated fresh flows.

For I1 issuer-validation tests on upstream SAML IdPs, the provider trust is established from exchanged metadata (metadata XML or metadata URL). The fuzzer MUST configure the SAML provider with explicit metadata from the intended IdP; otherwise issuer/certificate expectations are undefined and issuer-mismatch results are uninterpretable.

For I1 signature-substitution tests on upstream SAML IdPs, trust anchors come from metadata/certificates exchanged during provider setup. The fuzzer MUST keep provider metadata fixed while mutating only the runtime SAMLResponse signature material; changing metadata/certificates is an admin-authorized trust change, not a proof-integrity failure.

ZITADEL userinfo returns claims only according to granted scopes. The fuzzer MUST request the scopes needed for identity verification (for example profile/email and any reserved scopes for roles or metadata) before using verify_granted_identity as an oracle; absent claims due to missing scope are not security failures.

Reserved organization scopes have exact semantic meaning, not wildcard matching. In particular, urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} enforces membership in the selected organization, and urn:zitadel:iam:org:domain:primary:{domainname} enforces both organization membership and username suffix by the provided domain. For multi-identity I4 tests, the fuzzer MUST omit these scopes unless intentionally testing organization/domain binding; they are not pattern fields and '*' would be literal text if sent.

For multi-tenant SAML/SSO tests, if organization-specific login settings override defaults, the fuzzer MUST send the organization scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} in the authorization request to select the intended org context. Otherwise ZITADEL uses default settings and the wrong IdP/login policy may be exercised.

Token exchange audience is restrictive: requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. For I5 audience-escalation tests, the fuzzer MUST first obtain baseline tokens whose audience already includes the target project/client when testing allowed exchanges, and MUST expect rejection when requesting any new audience outside that combined set.

Token exchange scope can differ from the input token, but invalid or excessive scope returns invalid_scope. For I5 scope-escalation tests, the fuzzer MUST compare the exchanged token's actual returned scope/claims against the requested expansion and not assume the request was honored verbatim.

When requested_token_type is urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token in token exchange, ZITADEL returns the ID token in the access_token field and token_type=N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT use that returned access_token as a Bearer API credential; use requested_token_type access_token or jwt plus openid scope if both API credential and ID token are needed.

ZITADEL rejects expired ID tokens used as subject_token in token exchange. For I2 freshness tests involving token exchange with id_token subject tokens, the fuzzer SHOULD use a valid control token first and interpret rejection of expired ID tokens as by-design.

JWT/private_key_jwt assertions used for client authentication or JWT profile grants have a documented freshness bound: iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour, aud MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain, and kid must identify the configured key. The fuzzer MUST satisfy these preconditions in control requests before attributing failures to the tested invariant.

For I2 token-freshness tests on OAuth/OIDC tokens, the sequence MUST include a control login using a valid token/assertion (for example exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}, iat={{now_epoch}} where applicable) alongside the attack login. Without a control, LOGIN_FAILED cannot be distinguished from broken client authentication or grant setup.

The introspection endpoint reports active=true only if the token is active and the requesting client is part of the token audience. The fuzzer MUST authenticate introspection as a client/API that is in the token audience; otherwise active=false or 401 invalid_client is not evidence of token invalidity.

ZITADEL uses opaque access tokens by default. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume local JWT parsing is possible for session tokens returned by code flow or refresh flow unless the application is explicitly configured for JWT access tokens or token exchange requested_token_type=jwt is used.

For I5 tests involving user metadata claims, values in urn:zitadel:iam:user:metadata are base64 encoded. The fuzzer MUST decode before semantic comparison; raw base64 differences are not authorization-binding failures.

For I4/I5 tests that rely on automatic user creation from external SAML IdPs, Login V2 user creation fails unless required fields are populated from IdP attributes, typically via an Actions V2 response manipulation on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent. The fuzzer MUST ensure required attributes (email, first/last name, username as needed) are mapped, or login failure is a setup issue rather than a security result.

If external IdP login is not enabled in the applicable login policy, SAML broker login will be unavailable. The fuzzer MUST ensure 'External Login allowed' is enabled on the default or organization login policy before running SAML broker tests.

ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flow. The fuzzer MUST initiate the flow first and bind any forged SAMLResponse to the issued request/RelayState/InResponseTo context; unsolicited IdP-initiated responses are not a valid test setup.

For SAML tests against ZITADEL as broker/SP, the executor MUST use the ACS-intent/programmatic flow semantics: initiate the SAML flow, preserve RelayState, and ensure the response matches the original request ID. Sending a standalone fabricated SAMLResponse without prior initiation will be rejected for flow reasons, not security reasons.

The SAML SSO endpoint returns HTTP 200 even on SAML-level errors; failure is conveyed inside the SAML StatusCode/message. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat HTTP 200 from /saml/v2/SSO as successful authentication by itself.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution default-config testing, ZITADEL documentation states trust is established from exchanged metadata/certificates and best practice is to validate signatures and parties. The fuzzer MUST configure a real provider trust relationship first; acceptance of attacker-signed assertions without matching configured metadata/cert is the relevant oracle, not mere presence of a Signature element.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch and related issuer/audience tests, the fuzzer MUST distinguish ZITADEL's two SAML roles. /saml/v2/SSO is ZITADEL acting as IdP for downstream SPs, while SAML identity-brokering tests target ZITADEL consuming upstream IdP assertions via configured external IdPs. Do not interpret downstream IdP endpoint behavior as upstream broker validation behavior.

For I2 saml_assertion_id_replay and saml_one_time_use_replay, include a control login with a fresh assertion first. A replay rejection/failure must be compared against a known-good baseline because ZITADEL SAML flows are session/request-bound and malformed flow state can also cause rejection.

For I2 expired assertion tests, use a control login in the same provider/app setup before sending an expired assertion. Otherwise a failed login may reflect missing provider mapping, missing required attributes for user creation, or disabled external login policy rather than NotOnOrAfter enforcement.

SAML broker logins may fail by design if required user fields are not mapped from upstream SAML attributes. For I1/I2/I4/I5 SAML broker tests, the fuzzer MUST ensure upstream assertions provide required attributes (for example email/firstName/lastName or equivalent action-based mapping) so failures are attributable to security checks rather than provisioning failure.

External IdP login is gated by login policy. For any SAML broker test, the fuzzer MUST enable 'External Login allowed' on the relevant instance or organization before attempting SAML authentication, otherwise login failure is expected and not evidence of secure rejection.

Organization scoping is controlled by reserved scopes such as urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id}. If organization-specific login settings or IdPs are configured, the fuzzer MUST send the organization scope in the authorization request; otherwise ZITADEL may use default settings and the wrong IdP/policy, causing false positives in cross-tenant and cross-provider tests.

Token exchange audience is restrictive by design: requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject and actor tokens. Cross-project or cross-organization token exchange attempts outside that combined audience should be expected to fail; the fuzzer must provision subject/actor tokens with the target audience in baseline setups before testing for audience-binding bypass.

Token exchange scope can legitimately differ from the original request because ZITADEL allows changing scope, but invalid or excessive scope should be rejected. For I5 scope-escalation tests, compare requested scope against the documented rule that invalid_scope is returned when requested scope exceeds what is granted by the resource owner.

When requested_token_type=id_token in token exchange, ZITADEL returns the ID token in the access_token field and token_type=N_A by design. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat that returned value as a bearer API credential or as an authorization-binding violation.

ZITADEL rejects expired ID tokens used as subject_token in token exchange. For freshness tests involving token exchange with ID tokens, expired-token rejection is expected behavior and should not be confused with broader replay protection semantics.

The resource parameter in token exchange is currently unsupported and always results in invalid_target. The fuzzer MUST NOT use resource to model audience tests on ZITADEL; use the audience parameter instead.

For JWT-based client authentication to token/introspection endpoints, iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour and aud MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain. Freshness or issuer/audience failures in these client assertions are setup errors unless intentionally under test.

ZITADEL's introspection endpoint reports active=true only if the token is active AND the requesting client is part of the token audience. The fuzzer MUST use an introspecting client that is in the token audience for control checks; otherwise active=false is expected and not evidence of revocation or freshness failure.

Opaque access tokens are the default in ZITADEL. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume local JWT inspection is always possible after login or token exchange; use introspection or userinfo as appropriate. A missing JWT claim in an opaque token is by design, not an authorization-binding bug.
For OIDC authorization requests used around SAML-brokered login, openid scope is mandatory. Missing openid causes invalid_scope and is a setup failure, not a security rejection.

Nonce is mandatory for implicit flow and is used to bind the client session to the ID token for replay mitigation. For any OIDC implicit-flow control or SSO-related freshness test, the fuzzer MUST send nonce and verify nonce-dependent behavior separately from SAML behavior.

JWKS keys may rotate without prior notice and clients are expected to refresh cached keys. For any trust-anchor rotation or stale-key coherence test, acceptance of a newly configured key is by design; only continued acceptance of an old key after explicit rotation and cache refresh window is relevant.

ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flow. The fuzzer MUST initiate login through the SP flow first and MUST NOT treat IdP-initiated SAML as supported. For forged SAML tests, preserve the SP-issued request context (especially InResponseTo/RelayState) when posting the SAMLResponse.

The SAML SSO endpoint documents that errors still return HTTP 200 and are expressed inside the SAML StatusCode/message. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat HTTP 200 from /saml/v2/SSO as success by itself; success/failure must be determined from the returned SAMLResponse content or from the downstream OIDC/token flow outcome.

For I1 SAML signature-validation tests (saml_cert_substitution, saml_unsigned_assertion, saml_spurious_signature, saml_post_binding_unsigned_assertion), ZITADEL as broker consumes upstream SAML assertions from configured external IdPs. A valid test setup MUST create and activate a SAML provider first; otherwise failures may reflect missing provider configuration rather than signature enforcement.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, issuer trust is derived from the configured SAML provider metadata/entity information. The fuzzer MUST compare behavior between a correctly configured provider and a mutated assertion issuer; do not interpret generic provider-not-found or mapping failures as proof of issuer validation.

For I2 SAML replay tests, use the same assertion identifier across two saml_login events and keep the same SP-initiated flow context shape. Because ZITADEL only supports SP-initiated SAML, replay tests that skip flow initiation or alter request correlation can fail for coherence reasons instead of replay protection.

For I2 expired SAML assertion tests, include a control login through the same provider without expired conditions before sending the expired assertion. Without a control, rejection may be caused by missing attribute mapping, disabled provider, or login-policy configuration rather than NotOnOrAfter enforcement.

For I3 config-change tests involving external SAML IdPs, activating/deactivating providers or changing login policy is BY DESIGN expected to affect subsequent logins immediately. A valid coherence test must show inconsistent handling of the same effective configuration, not merely that an admin changed provider availability or trust settings.

For I3 saml_mfa_bypass_via_binding_rule tests, ZITADEL's external IdP login path may require separate login-policy and action-based user provisioning setup. The fuzzer MUST first establish a working baseline for both password login and SAML login for the same user before concluding MFA bypass.

For I4 identity-binding tests on SAML brokering, user creation in Login V2 can fail unless required fields are mapped from IdP attributes via Actions V2 on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent. The fuzzer MUST ensure required attributes such as email/given_name/family_name are supplied or mapped; otherwise failed or fallback account creation is a setup error, not an identity-binding result.

ZITADEL commonly derives the local login/display identity from external attributes such as email/username rather than preserving the raw SAML NameID verbatim. For I4 collision tests, compare stable identifiers (e.g. sub/user id) and account-link outcomes, not only raw display strings.

For I4 unverified_email_account_linking tests, documentation shows actions can explicitly set EmailVerified during external authentication. The fuzzer MUST control whether email_verified is asserted/mapped; otherwise automatic profile manipulation may mask or create linking behavior unrelated to broker core logic.

For I5 token exchange audience tests, ZITADEL documents that requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject and actor tokens. The fuzzer MUST first mint subject/actor tokens whose audiences intentionally include or exclude the target audience; otherwise rejection is expected by design and not evidence of a bug.

For I5 token exchange scope-escalation tests, ZITADEL allows requested scope to differ from supplied tokens and then validates it. The oracle MUST inspect the returned scope field and resulting claims, not assume the requested scope was granted verbatim.

For I5 token exchange resource tests, the resource parameter is currently not supported and supplying it should yield invalid_target behavior. The fuzzer MUST NOT interpret resource-based failures as audience-binding vulnerabilities.

When requesting requested_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token in token exchange, ZITADEL returns the ID token in the access_token field and token_type=N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT use that returned access_token as a Bearer session token for subsequent API calls.

For token exchange using subject_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt, ZITADEL only allows self-signed JWT subject tokens in combination with a valid actor_token for impersonation. The fuzzer MUST include actor_token for this path; otherwise rejection is expected by design.

For JWT-based client authentication on token or introspection endpoints, the client assertion iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour and aud MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain. Use dynamic values such as iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} in generated assertions.

For OIDC authorization requests used around SAML-brokered login, nonce MUST be provided for implicit flow and is recommended for code flow to bind the client session to the ID token. The fuzzer SHOULD include nonce and state in control and attack requests to avoid replay/CSRF-related false positives.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Zitadel management API uses REST gateway paths under /management/v1/ (org-scoped). Do NOT use gRPC Connect paths. For IdP setup: create_provider creates the IdP, enable_auth_method adds it to the login policy with ownerType='IDP_OWNER_TYPE_ORG' (NOT 'ORG' or 'OWNER_TYPE_ORG'). Both are needed before IdP login works. SAML login is brokered — saml_login is NOT directly callable as a standalone POST. It is handled internally by the executor's ZITADEL-LOGIN flow triggered via start_oidc_auth with scope containing urn:zitadel:iam:org:idp:id:{idp_id}.
